observation_or_problem: Needed a specific, falsifiable hypothesis before API credentials would be issued.
action_or_experiment: Reviewed the Massive API documentation and drafted a research proposal around clustered insider buying, including a fundamentals-based health filter (debt-to-equity).
result: Proposal submitted naming Form 4 filings, price aggregates, and fundamentals (market_cap, debt_to_equity) as the intended datasets.
decision: Submit proposal and await API credentials before touching real data.

observation_or_problem: No working pipeline existed yet for the proposed hypothesis.
action_or_experiment: Author used Google Gemini to generate and edit the original five-module pipeline baseline: universe scanner, data client, signal engine, backtester, orchestrator.
result: Basic end-to-end run worked on placeholder logic.
decision: Proceed to wire in real Massive API data and real filters.

observation_or_problem: README lacked setup and quickstart detail for a reproducible pipeline.
action_or_experiment: Author used Google Gemini to help rewrite README with quickstart, configuration, and pipeline-component documentation.
result: Clear setup instructions now exist for a new environment.
decision: Keep README as a living document, update as modules change.

observation_or_problem: Repo tracked cache/venv/editor files that should never be committed.
action_or_experiment: Cleaned up and expanded .gitignore for a standard Python project.
result: .env, data/, venv, and cache directories excluded from version control.
decision: Keep .gitignore current as new local-only paths appear.

observation_or_problem: Phase 1 (16 hand-picked tickers) looked profitable in an early smoke test.
action_or_experiment: Reviewed how the 16 tickers were chosen.
result: Selection was manual and too small a sample to trust; a clear selection bias risk.
decision: Reject Phase 1, move to a dynamically discovered full-market universe.

observation_or_problem: Phase 2 (~5,500-ticker universe, no filters) showed near-zero Sharpe and a max gain of +33,580%.
action_or_experiment: Inspected the outlier trades driving the absurd max gain.
result: Unadjusted stock splits were corrupting raw price data for several tickers.
decision: Add a data-quality guard before trusting any full-universe run again.

observation_or_problem: Needed to confirm the split-corruption fix actually worked.
action_or_experiment: Added a $5 MIN_PRICE floor and re-ran the full universe.
result: Split distortion resolved, but mean return and Sharpe stayed flat-to-negative on 60/90-day holds.
decision: Keep investigating filters; a price floor alone is not sufficient.

observation_or_problem: Still no configuration produced a positive edge at any holding period.
action_or_experiment: Added a $100k minimum cluster value and a trailing stop from entry (Phase 4).
result: Noise trades cut by 87%, but mean return and Sharpe stayed negative everywhere, and win rate decayed from 30 to 90 days.
decision: Diagnose root cause before adding more filters: insiders are naturally contrarian, fixed-time exits let spikes decay, trailing stops whipsaw on gap-downs.

observation_or_problem: Raw insider clustering had no notion of routine vs. opportunistic buying.
action_or_experiment: Added opportunistic-vs-routine insider classification (Cohen/Malloy/Pomorski) and self-relative conviction sizing, tested on real Massive data.
result: Filters wired correctly, but the first full-market real-data run still returned negative Sharpe at every holding period.
decision: Signal is not real yet; keep refining rather than reverting to placeholder logic.

observation_or_problem: Wanted to test an earnings-proximity timing filter.
action_or_experiment: Wired fetch_short_interest and fetch_earnings into the data client and attempted to use both.
result: fetch_earnings() always returns empty; the account's Massive plan lacks the Benzinga earnings entitlement.
decision: Drop the earnings-proximity idea for lack of data; keep the short-interest feed.

observation_or_problem: Insider buying alone was a weak, noisy contrarian signal.
action_or_experiment: Required short-side days-to-cover >= a threshold at signal time; swept 1.0/2.0/3.0/5.0.
result: 2.0 won on both train and test Sharpe.
decision: Adopt MIN_DAYS_TO_COVER = 2.0.

observation_or_problem: A trailing-stop-only exit still produced negative Sharpe at every holding period.
action_or_experiment: Tested 4 exit variations at 15%/30%: trail-only, trail+take-profit, fixed-stop+take-profit, fixed-stop-only.
result: Fixed 15% stop-loss + fixed 30% take-profit (no trailing) was the only configuration positive at every holding period.
decision: Adopt STOP_LOSS_PCT=0.15, TAKE_PROFIT_PCT=0.30, TRAILING_STOP=False as the new default exit rule.

observation_or_problem: Backtest ignored trading costs, an unrealistic assumption.
action_or_experiment: Added a 20 bps round-trip transaction cost (TRANSACTION_COST_PCT=0.002).
result: Edge shrank substantially but stayed positive at every holding period.
decision: Keep 0.002 as the standing cost assumption for every later experiment.

observation_or_problem: Worried the surviving edge was a fluke of the tuning window.
action_or_experiment: Ran a train (<=2024-06-30) / test (>=2024-07-01) walk-forward split at this stage.
result: Result was mixed and weak, at or below the noise floor.
decision: Treat the edge as unconfirmed; keep refining before trusting it.

observation_or_problem: Wanted to see if the stronger MIN_DAYS_TO_COVER filter changed the walk-forward read.
action_or_experiment: Raised MIN_DAYS_TO_COVER from 1.0 to 2.0 and repeated the same train/test split.
result: Edge held its sign on both train and test for the first time in the project.
decision: Upgrade the read from leans-toward-noise to a real but weak edge; proceed to universe filters.

observation_or_problem: Wanted to test whether a liquidity/quality floor would help, not just insider filters.
action_or_experiment: Added a $5 price floor and a $1M 20-day dollar-volume floor.
result: Turned every holding period negative (60-day total return went from +16.8% to -9.2%).
decision: Reject the liquidity floor; keep MIN_PRICE=0.0 and MIN_DOLLAR_VOLUME=0.0. Edge concentrates in micro-caps.

observation_or_problem: Had not yet tried the opposite of a liquidity floor: an upper ceiling to keep only the thinnest names.
action_or_experiment: Swept a MAX_DOLLAR_VOLUME ceiling: None / $29M / $12M / $2.5M.
result: $12M looked good on train (Sharpe 0.064) but went negative on test (-0.058), an overfitting warning. $2.5M held up on both train and test; 60-day max drawdown fell from -38.3% to -10.5%, total return rose from +16.8% to +22.4%, portfolio Sharpe roughly tripled to 1.189.
decision: Adopt MAX_DOLLAR_VOLUME = 2,500,000, the biggest single improvement found in the project so far.

observation_or_problem: Wanted to check whether a price floor helps once the new dollar-volume ceiling is in place.
action_or_experiment: Retested the $5 MIN_PRICE floor on top of the $2.5M ceiling.
result: Hurt badly again; test Sharpe went negative at every holding period.
decision: Keep MIN_PRICE=0.0 disabled; the edge is confirmed to concentrate below $5/share.

observation_or_problem: Wanted to know if any single trade-level feature could justify extra position sizing.
action_or_experiment: Ran a correlation check: cluster size, conviction ratio, days-to-cover, dollar volume, and entry price against trade_return.
result: Every feature came in under 0.02 correlation with trade_return.
decision: Drop feature-based size tilting; no usable signal in these features.

observation_or_problem: Static position sizing never let the account compound gains.
action_or_experiment: Added mode="compound" (position size = current equity x position_size_pct) and swept the base rate 2%-15%.
result: Compounding beat static sizing on both return and Sharpe with no extra drawdown; the base-rate sweep showed Sharpe never changes under pure compounding, since it scales the whole return stream proportionally.
decision: Adopt compounding as the new sizing default, pending the house-money comparison below.

observation_or_problem: Wanted more upside from winning streaks without risking more of the original stake.
action_or_experiment: Added mode="house_money", splitting equity into protected principal (sized at position_size_pct) and a profit cushion above initial capital (sized at a higher aggressive_pct); swept aggressive_pct 0.05-0.20.
result: 0.08 gave the best Sharpe at every holding period for almost no extra drawdown, an actual improvement in curve shape, not just a rescaling.
decision: Adopt SIZING_MODE="house_money", HOUSE_MONEY_AGGRESSIVE_PCT=0.08 as the default.

observation_or_problem: Wanted an independent check that POSITION_SIZE_PCT=0.02 was not an arbitrary conservative guess.
action_or_experiment: Computed full-Kelly (4.4%-5.9% depending on holding period) and half-Kelly (2.7%-3.0%), and separately derived a ~2.56% capital ceiling from the actual maximum concurrent open positions (39 at 60-day).
result: Half-Kelly and the independently derived capacity ceiling agree closely; using half-Kelly as the base rate did not improve on 2%, it just scaled return and drawdown up together.
decision: Keep POSITION_SIZE_PCT=0.02 as a capital-realistic choice, confirmed rather than merely assumed.

observation_or_problem: This universe runs near-permanently crowded, averaging ~21 concurrent open positions.
action_or_experiment: Tested concurrency-throttle sizing: dividing new-trade size by (1 + decay_rate x num_open_positions).
result: Even mild decay cut total return by more than half for almost no Sharpe benefit.
decision: Reject concurrency-throttle sizing; not adopted.

observation_or_problem: Wondered if blending the 30/60/90-day sleeves would reduce volatility.
action_or_experiment: Tested splitting capital a third each across the 30/60/90-day holding-period sleeves.
result: Underperformed the single best sleeve alone on both return and Sharpe, since the weakest sleeve drags the blend down.
decision: Reject blending; keep a single-sleeve default.

observation_or_problem: A plain trailing stop had already been rejected, but the universe had since changed (the $2.5M ceiling).
action_or_experiment: Built a profit-activated trail (stays at the fixed stop until a trade is up trail_activation_pct, then trails at trail_pct, with the 30% take-profit still active as backstop) and swept activation 10%-80%.
result: 50% activation / 15% trail is a clear peak: 60-day portfolio Sharpe rose from 1.280 to 2.139, total return from +31.8% to +109.4%, for only a small extra drawdown. A diagnostic showed only 32-46 of ~890 trades per period actually use the trail, and win rate barely moved.
decision: Adopt TRAIL_ACTIVATION_PCT=0.50, TRAIL_PCT=0.15, confirmed as a genuine local peak via a fine grid around 40%-70%.

observation_or_problem: Wanted to know if a more elaborate exit mechanic could beat the plain activation trail.
action_or_experiment: Designed and tested 6 further ideas: no take-profit cap, two-stage partial exit, ratcheting trail width, ATR-based trail, time-gated activation, liquidity-tiered targets.
result: The best of these (ratcheting trail width, Sharpe 1.589) still fell well short of the plain activation trail.
decision: None adopted; keep the simpler mechanic.

observation_or_problem: User preferred a lower-risk setting over the data-optimal one.
action_or_experiment: Set TRAIL_ACTIVATION_PCT=0.30 per explicit user instruction.
result: Lower risk, lower reward: 60-day Sharpe 1.276, total return 37.6%, versus 2.139/+109.4% at 50%.
decision: Apply the user's choice; revisit later once more evidence (the stop-loss sweep) is in hand.

observation_or_problem: Wanted to see whether a wider stop-loss changes the activation trade-off, and whether to keep the 30% detour.
action_or_experiment: Swept fixed stop-loss 10%/15%/20%/25% crossed with trail activation.
result: Widening 15%->20% at 30-day/50%-activation lifts total return from 103.3% to 132.3% for only a small extra drawdown (Sharpe 2.107->2.088); the same widening hurts 60-day, since STOP_LOSS_PCT and TRAIL_ACTIVATION_PCT are single global settings shared by every holding period; 25% pushes return higher but Sharpe and drawdown both keep degrading.
decision: Reverse the 30%-activation detour; adopt STOP_LOSS_PCT=0.20 with TRAIL_ACTIVATION_PCT=0.50 as the 30-day-primary configuration.

observation_or_problem: An independent, entry-date-ordered, capital-constrained simulator built for validation disagreed with the production numbers (113.7%/1.986 vs. reported 132.3%/2.088), despite zero trades ever being skipped for lack of cash.
action_or_experiment: Audited simulate_dynamic() in portfolio_simulator.py.
result: Found it sized every trade using equity computed in exit-date order, letting a trade's size be inflated by a different trade that entered later but happened to close first, a look-ahead in the compounding schedule affecting every dynamic sizing mode used all session.
decision: Refactor portfolio_simulator.py around a shared entry-date-ordered engine (_run_entry_ordered); re-run the full pipeline to confirm the corrected numbers.

observation_or_problem: config.py's stop-loss comment still cited pre-fix performance numbers.
action_or_experiment: Updated the comment text to stop citing stale figures.
result: Config self-documentation is now consistent with the fixed engine.
decision: Keep in-code comments in sync with the code whenever a fix changes reported numbers.

observation_or_problem: A full code review found process_single_ticker() swallowing every exception silently (except Exception: return empty DataFrame), masking a real per-ticker bug as a legitimate no-signal result.
action_or_experiment: Added a warning print naming the ticker and the exception type/message before returning the empty frame.
result: A live pipeline re-run confirmed the fix changed no numbers (113.68% return, 1.986 Sharpe, exactly as predicted) and printed zero warnings, meaning no ticker is currently failing silently.
decision: Keep the fix; treat silent exception handling as a standing code-review check.

observation_or_problem: The assignment requires a research report, a decision log and experiment record in CSV, and an AI/source disclosure inside the repository, none of which existed yet, and the original sweep scripts had only ever run in a temporary scratchpad that has since been cleared.
action_or_experiment: Wrote research_report.md, this decision log and experiment_record.csv from specs/decision_journal.md, added an Assistance and source disclosure section to README.md, and rebuilt the exit/sizing sweep and the validation suite as committed, reusable scripts under experiments/.
result: Both experiment scripts reproduce the headline 30-day numbers end to end from cached data (see experiments/exit_and_sizing_results.csv and experiments/validation_results.csv).
decision: Hold everything unstaged for review before any commit, per explicit instruction.
